summary: This experimental RFC defines ALPN extensions for RADIUS over TLS and DTLS so peers can negotiate a RADIUS variant called "RADIUS/1.1". It is meant to remove the dependency on the MD5 hash used by older RADIUS. RADIUS/UDP and RADIUS/TCP are not changed.

plainLanguage.summary: RADIUS/1.1 is a transport profile negotiated over TLS or DTLS using ALPN. When both peers choose it, they do not use the older shared-secret and MD5 methods for packet authentication or attribute obfuscation.

subtitle: An ALPN-negotiated RADIUS profile that removes packet-level MD5 use over TLS and DTLS.

tldr.problem: RADIUS over TLS and DTLS still used MD5-based packet authentication and attribute obfuscation, even though the transport already provided security.
tldr.mechanism: Peers negotiate the RADIUS/1.1 transport profile with ALPN, stop using the RADIUS shared secret for packet authentication, and remove the old MD5-based obfuscation methods.
tldr.outcome: The Experimental RFC updates several RADIUS specifications; it does not change RADIUS over UDP or TCP.

today: RFC 9765 is Experimental. The unit metadata says it updates RFCs 2865, 2866, 5176, 6613, 6614, and 7360.

sections.title: Removing MD5 from Protected RADIUS Links
sections.content:
RADIUS uses MD5 with a shared secret to authenticate packets and obscure some attributes. RADIUS over TLS and DTLS had retained those packet-level methods inside the protected transport.

This RFC defines RADIUS/1.1 as a transport profile that removes those MD5 uses. It does not revise RADIUS over UDP or TCP, and it is not a wholesale replacement for the RADIUS protocol.
sections.plainLanguage: Older RADIUS packet rules continued to use MD5 even inside TLS or DTLS. RADIUS/1.1 removes those packet-level uses when the peers agree to the new profile.

sections.title: Negotiating RADIUS/1.1 with ALPN
sections.content:
During the TLS handshake, a client lists the application protocols it supports using Application-Layer Protocol Negotiation (ALPN). The server chooses a supported option, and both sides use RADIUS/1.1 only when the ALPN name radius/1.1 is selected.

The profile requires TLS 1.3 or later. Implementations can allow both the historic profile and RADIUS/1.1, or be configured to require RADIUS/1.1; when no ALPN negotiation selects it, RADIUS/1.1 must not be used.
sections.plainLanguage: The client and server choose a RADIUS version during the TLS handshake. They use RADIUS/1.1 only if both negotiate the name radius/1.1.

sections.title: Packet and Attribute Changes
sections.content:
The RADIUS packet header stays the same size, but fields that previously carried authenticators are repurposed to carry an opaque token for matching requests and responses. The profile removes the Message-Authenticator attribute from packets and ignores it if received.

Attributes that were obscured with MD5, such as User-Password and Tunnel-Password, are sent using their ordinary text or octet encodings inside TLS. Other attributes keep their existing meaning and encoding unless the RFC specifically changes their handling.
sections.plainLanguage: The packet header keeps its size, while a token identifies matching requests and replies. Password attributes no longer use the old MD5 obfuscation because TLS protects the connection.

sections.title: Security, Privacy, and Scope
sections.content:
Using this profile removes specified MD5 uses from the RADIUS packet layer; it does not require or prohibit any particular authentication method carried inside RADIUS. A server that removes all MD5 use cannot support CHAP or other methods that depend on MD5.

Only the client and server on a negotiated connection need to know that the profile is active. RADIUS/UDP and RADIUS/TCP are unchanged. The RFC updates earlier RADIUS specifications only for connections using this profile and is published as Experimental.
sections.plainLanguage: RADIUS/1.1 changes packet protection, not every authentication method that RADIUS can carry. It applies to negotiated TLS or DTLS connections; UDP and TCP RADIUS remain unchanged.
